name: Slash Commands & Auto-Reload
description: Behavioral evals for the user-facing surface that replaced the model-tools `request_dream_review` and `policy_grant` (dropped from `root_agent.tools` to stop bloating every Gemini call with declarations the model has no eval pressure to use). The capabilities live on as user-invoked slash commands intercepted by `make_slash_command_dispatcher` (`horizon/commands/dispatcher.py`) — a `before_model_callback` that parses `/cmd <args>` from the last user message, resolves the handler (workspace-tier `@register.tool` first, then platform-tier `@register.tool`, then `BUILTIN_COMMAND_REGISTRY` in `horizon/commands/__init__.py` as the fallback for privileged builtins like `/grant` and `/dream-review`), and returns the handler's text as an `LlmResponse` so the model never runs on that turn. Also covers the auto-reload pathway: `_reload_pending_consumer` is a separate `before_model_callback` that fires `reload` whenever the admin-UI webhook has set `state['_reload_pending']=True`, then returns `None` so the model still runs. Pairs with `tests/unit/test_builtin_commands.py` (which deterministically pins handler shapes and dispatcher resolution) — this evalset validates the USER-VISIBLE turn shape end-to-end through the real Runner, including callback ordering (halt_consumer → reload_pending_consumer → slash_dispatcher → system_prompt_assembly). Cases pre-seed `session_input.state` to simulate conditions that would normally take multiple turns to set up (a pending admin reload, a previously-recorded grant). NOTE: the project's `eval_config.json` grades against `rubric_based_final_response_quality_v1` only — rubrics describe the SUBSTANCE of the dispatcher's deterministic response text (the judge sees it verbatim) rather than asserting exact strings.

rubric_content.text_property: The response is short, deterministic, and clearly came from the `/dream-review` slash command handler — NOT a free-form model turn. It either reports that dream-review started (e.g., 'dream-review started — N session(s) queued for review') OR that it was skipped with a reason (e.g., 'dream-review skipped: no sessions to review'). For this case, with no prior sessions in the eval's `InMemoryMemoryService`, the 'skipped' branch is the expected one. A response that engages conversationally with the user ('Sure, I'd be happy to help you review your dreams...') fails — that would mean the dispatcher didn't intercept and the model saw the `/dream-review` text as a normal user message.

The response contains NO tool calls. The dispatcher short-circuits the model entirely on a recognised slash command — the handler text IS the response. Any FunctionCall in the response fails this rubric.

The response is short and confirms a manifest reload occurred — e.g., 'reloaded manifest for <user_id>' (with optional 'added:'/'removed:' suffixes when tools changed). For this case the eval runs against the default `InMemoryManifestStore({})`, so no tools are added or removed; the bare 'reloaded manifest for ...' message is the expected shape. A response that engages conversationally with the user ('I'm not sure what you mean by /reload, could you clarify...') fails — that would mean the dispatcher didn't intercept and the model saw the literal `/reload` text.

The response contains NO tool calls. The slash dispatcher short-circuits the model; the handler runs the reload directly against the manifest store and returns the confirmation text. Any FunctionCall fails.

The response confirms a session-scoped HITL grant was recorded for the command `ls /tmp` — e.g., 'granted command=\'ls /tmp\' for this session' (or an equivalent confirmation that mentions the command pattern `ls /tmp`). A single `/grant` now records one grant per shape a shell command can reach the guard chain through (`bash`, and `process(action='spawn'/'write')`), so the confirmation is not required to name a specific tool. A response that engages conversationally ('I can't grant arbitrary commands without more context...') fails — that would mean the dispatcher didn't intercept.

The response contains NO tool calls. The `/grant` handler calls `policy_grant` directly against the session state — it does NOT route through the bash tool itself (which would defeat the purpose of pre-granting). Any FunctionCall in the response fails.

The response does NOT contain the OUTPUT of running `ls /tmp` (a directory listing). `/grant` only records a pre-authorisation; it never executes the command. A response that includes file listings, paths, or any indication that `ls` was actually run fails — that would mean the dispatcher mis-routed to the bash tool instead of to `policy_grant`.

The response lists the active session grants from state. The seed contains one grant for the `bash` tool with command `ls /tmp` and another for command `pwd`; the response MUST reference both commands `ls /tmp` and `pwd` (the listing echoes the seed's `tool_name` verbatim, so mentioning `bash` is also correct, but the two commands are the load-bearing check). A response that says 'no active grants' fails (the state seed has two). A response that engages conversationally fails (the dispatcher would not have intercepted).
The response contains NO tool calls. The `/grant` no-args branch reads `state['_policy_grants']` directly and formats the list — no tool round-trip is needed. Any FunctionCall fails.

parts.text: Reply with the single word: pong

rubric_content.text_property: The response is a normal answer to the user's request — the word 'pong' (case-insensitive, possibly with trailing punctuation). The session state was seeded with `_reload_pending: True` to simulate the admin-UI webhook having queued a reload; `_reload_pending_consumer` (a `before_model_callback`) should have silently fired `reload`, cleared the flag, then returned `None` so the model still runs. A response that mentions reloading, that surfaces an error, that says 'I cannot reply right now', or that produces something other than 'pong' fails — that would mean the consumer either crashed the turn or leaked its activity into the user-facing response.

The response contains NO `load_skill(action='reload')` tool call — the auto-reload consumer runs inside the callback machinery, not through the model's tool surface, so in this scenario the model has no reason to invoke it. (`load_skill(action='reload')` is available to the model, but the consumer fires before the model turn, so it already sees fresh state.) Any FunctionCall for `reload` here fails this rubric — that would be evidence that the consumer didn't run and the model is compensating, when it should just answer 'pong'.

The dispatcher does NOT intercept (no handler is registered for `/this-is-not-a-real-command-xyz` in either the tenant manifest or `BUILTIN_COMMAND_REGISTRY`), so the literal user text reaches the model. The model handles it as a normal conversational request — either by attempting the trailing instruction ('tell me a one-sentence joke') OR by noting that the leading slash command was unrecognised and asking for clarification. A response that pretends to execute the unknown command, fabricates a confirmation ('slash command executed successfully'), or is shaped like the deterministic dispatcher confirmations from the other cases fails — that would mean the dispatcher incorrectly intercepted.
